summary: Flotilla is a dense, brain-burning economic engine-builder where players split time between exploring/gathering as a "Sinkside" captain and building up the flotilla as a "Skyside" commissioner, with a shared market and interlocking economies tying everyone together. It's a long, fiddly game (often running 2-4 hours) that rewards repeated plays once the two-layer system clicks, but the first game or two is largely spent just learning how the pieces interact.
praised: Strong post-apocalyptic nautical theme woven into mechanics (not just pasted on)
Shared market creates real tension — sales and purchases shift prices for everyone
Great long-term depth and variety of strategic paths (artifacts, quests, outposts, guild seals)
criticised: Very high learning curve; teaching requires explaining two interacting layers of rules
Long playtime that can stretch to 3-4 hours, especially early plays
Resources are abstract colors (red/green/blue/yellow) rather than thematic goods, which some find immersion-breaking
Not a game you can expect to optimize until several plays in

interaction.detail: Sinkside players gather resources that feed Skyside players' construction, and a shared, fluctuating market means every purchase or sale changes prices for the whole table. Positive actions frequently benefit other players as a side effect, and players compete for the same quests, guild seals, and outpost placements, so timing and reading opponents matters a lot.

scoring.how_you_win: Players alternate between commanding a ship exploring and salvaging the flooded world and investing back in building up the Flotilla's economy; the player who accumulates the most points from deliveries, construction, and completed contracts by game's end wins.
